subject.title: [Bug]: Native Talk button triggers OpenAI Realtime WebRTC call and fails with 500 when Realtime is not configured

question: Should browser Talk start when OpenAI Realtime is implicitly usable through OpenAI API-key/OAuth/Codex auth, or only when an explicit Talk realtime readiness/configuration says the provider is usable?
rationale: The current docs and code intentionally support implicit OpenAI/Codex realtime activation, while the reporter expects local/non-Realtime Talk configuration not to start OpenAI WebRTC; either answer changes user-facing setup semantics and upgrade expectations.

options.title: Gate On Gateway Readiness
options.body: Use `talk.catalog` or an equivalent Gateway preflight to disable/block Talk before microphone startup unless a usable realtime provider is ready, while preserving the chosen credential policy.

options.title: Keep Implicit Credential Activation
options.body: Treat configured OpenAI/Codex realtime auth as enough to show/start browser Talk and narrow the fix to better diagnostics for provider/API failures.

options.title: Require Explicit Realtime Config
options.body: Only show or start browser Talk when `talk.realtime` is explicitly configured, accepting any migration or upgrade impact for existing implicit-auth users.

recommendation.title: Gate On Gateway Readiness
recommendation.body: Use `talk.catalog` or an equivalent Gateway preflight to disable/block Talk before microphone startup unless a usable realtime provider is ready, while preserving the chosen credential policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the most recent OpenAI Realtime auth fallback/docs change and the current UI path by git history, so they are the best available owner for the product contract.
